answer: Sequential Work Receipts. Each new identity must complete a paid task whose output is checked against prior submissions; only fresh, non-redundant work earns the nectar reward. Duplicate outputs are rejected, so clones pay compute and fees without payout. The velvet edge: honest workers accumulate a haven of accepted receipts, while each marginal clone runs strictly negative-EV, since its expected reward falls below per-task cost plus registration overhead.
